title: Two Brothers Plan Safer Care With Their Father
script: Yusuf: [tired] Fikri, we need to discuss Father’s safety after his fall, but I do not want us to decide his life without him.
Fikri: [thoughtful] I agree. Has the clinic explained why he fell or what support he may need?
Yusuf: Not yet. He was treated for the injury, but a fuller assessment is booked for Thursday.
Fikri: [concerned] Good. My apartment is small and my work hours are long, so I cannot promise daily care alone.
Yusuf: That is an honest limit, not a lack of love. I have an extra room, but Father may prefer to stay near his neighbors.
Fikri: [reflective] Could he stay with you temporarily while we check safer options with him?
Yusuf: Yes, if he agrees. We can also ask about handrails, medicine review, transport, and support at home.
Fikri: I can attend appointments, manage a shared calendar, and cover part of any agreed care costs.
Yusuf: [warmly] I can handle mornings during the temporary stay. We should also plan breaks so neither of us becomes exhausted.
Fikri: What if Father refuses every change?
Yusuf: We listen to his reasons and explain the risks calmly. If his decision-making ability is in question, we ask qualified professionals for guidance.
Fikri: [gently] That is better than using one fall to remove all his independence.
Yusuf: Exactly. Safety matters, and so do dignity and choice.
Fikri: I felt guilty because I thought a good son should be available every hour.
Yusuf: [honestly] Reliable care is more important than an impossible promise. We can include relatives or paid support if Father accepts it.
Fikri: Then tonight we ask what he wants, explain what each of us can do, and write questions for the clinic.
Yusuf: We will make a temporary plan first and review it after the assessment.
Fikri: [relieved] I like that. No competition over who sacrifices more—just clear responsibilities and regular review.
Yusuf: And Father remains part of every decision that concerns him.
Fikri: [sincere] Agreed. Let us call him together and begin by listening.

quiz.question: What appointment is scheduled for Thursday?
options: A fuller assessment of the father’s needs

quiz.question: Why might the father prefer his current area?
quiz.explanation: His social connection matters to the choice.

quiz.question: What home changes may be discussed?
options: Handrails and other support at home
quiz.explanation: Safety options are considered before removing independence.

quiz.question: Why do the brothers plan breaks?
What type of plan will they make first?
options: A temporary plan reviewed after assessment
A medical plan written by the brothers

quiz.question: Why do the brothers need a new plan?
options: Their father wants to sell both apartments
Their father fell and his current home may not be safe
Fikri is leaving his job tomorrow
quiz.explanation: The fall triggers a safety review, not an automatic decision for him.

quiz.question: Who must be included before a final living decision?
options: Only the brother with the larger home
Their father and relevant health professionals
quiz.explanation: The plan respects the father’s voice and actual care needs.

quiz.question: What can Yusuf offer immediately?
options: A temporary room and help arranging an assessment
A promise that no further fall can happen
quiz.explanation: His offer is practical but does not exceed his role.

quiz.question: How can Fikri share responsibility?
options: Visit only when he feels guilty
Handle appointments, costs, visits, and parts of the weekly schedule
quiz.explanation: Care is divided into clear actions.

quiz.question: What does careful planning show?
options: The father has lost all independence
One son loves the father more
Family care never needs outside help
Love can include honest limits, consent, and reliable support
quiz.explanation: The dialogue rejects guilt as the only guide.
